title: Arkret String Profiles
description: Shared coarse-grained JSON Schema shapes for Arkret v1 string profiles. Custom format validation and UTF-8 octet limits are normative and require the SDK validator; JSON Schema patterns do not implement PRECIS, IDNA, or UTS #39.

human_identifier_localpart.description: Canonical RFC 8265 UsernameCaseMapped-derived localpart. Maximum 128 Unicode code points in prepared form.

agent_slug.description: Canonical controller-scoped Agent Agent selector slug. Maximum 64 Unicode code points in prepared form.

canonical_domain.description: Lowercase UTS #46 Nontransitional A-label domain with at least two labels; normative validation includes STD3, Bidi, Joiner, hyphen, DNS-length, and round-trip checks.

canonical_handle.description: Canonical <prepared-localpart>:<lowercase-A-label-domain> handle or realm alias. The prepared localpart maximum is 128 Unicode code points; the domain maximum is 253 ASCII octets.

acct_uri.description: RFC 7565 acct URI with UTF-8 localpart octets percent-encoded using uppercase hex when required, canonical A-label host, and no port.

single_line_display_text.description: NFC multilingual single-line display text; mixed scripts, emoji, and symbols are allowed.

display_text_128.description: Single-line display text limited to 128 Unicode code points in prepared form.

display_text_256.description: Single-line display text limited to 256 Unicode code points in prepared form.

display_text_512.description: Single-line display text limited to 512 Unicode code points in prepared form.

short_text.description: NFC multilingual short text. LF is allowed; CR, other C0/C1 controls, BOM, and bidi embedding/override controls are rejected.

audit_reason_text.description: Human-readable audit reason limited to 1024 Unicode code points. It is explanatory text only and never a machine-readable reason code or authorization source.

content_text.description: NFC multilingual content text; rendering contexts must escape markup and apply bidi isolation.

non_typed_identifier_floor.description: Lexical floor of every identifier value category that does NOT own the ak: namespace (opaque_correlation, document_local_symbol, external_system_identifier, registry_catalog_symbol, unregistered_object_identifier); see common-fields.md 2.1. The negative lookahead IS the floor: it mechanically proves the value cannot be an ak: typed id, which maxLength alone can never prove, while admitting every other value the field already accepted. It deliberately constrains nothing else - the per-field convergence direction (a registered typed kind, or a tighter opaque profile) is decided per object family, so a pattern-only floor composes with whatever profile the field already carries instead of pre-empting it.

bounded_non_typed_identifier.description: Nonempty bounded non-typed identifier shape. Length is at most 256 Unicode code points and the ak: typed-ID namespace is excluded. This definition supplies lexical constraints only; each owning scoped profile separately defines semantic category, scope and authority boundaries.

realm_action_name.description: Realm-owned action configuration name. The logical owner is the exact Realm, not an individual Event envelope or a Policy rule. Every carrier and update retains that same realm_id; first acceptance fixes (action, policy_scope), and later use must not rebind the name. The name alone is not a capability token, authorization subject, global object identity, or Event deduplication key.

membership_admission_handle.description: One failed-join admission lifecycle, scoped by its exact source and destination Realm, subject Account and covered join Event/RealmCommit. The handle only correlates the delegation, terminal certificate and one-use compensation binding. Authority remains the verified executor, signed delegation, terminal evidence and current membership cut; the handle alone grants no authority and never replaces Event identity or deduplication.

agent_confirmation_handle.description: One controller confirmation lifecycle for the exact Agent and pre-authored approved_event_id in the enclosing Realm. The handle correlates the immutable confirmation record; controller ActorId plus approval_nonce is the one-use admission coordinate. Controller authority, the exact signed Event, current authorization and nonce consumption remain mandatory. The handle alone is not an authorization bearer, principal identity, or Event deduplication key.

agent_draft_handle.description: One private pending-intent lifecycle under exact (controller_account_id, agent_id). Account Data and pending-intent carriers retain this same owner scope and the same UTF-8 literal; key derivation uses the registered domain-separated digests, not an alternate normalized identifier. The signed proposal, content commitment, accepted controller binding and source-gated CAS remain authority. The handle alone is not a principal identity, authorization bearer, or Event deduplication key.

media_focus_handle.description: One stable media focus lifecycle inside the exact Realm media-service configuration. Call, token, recording and exporter carriers retain the same realm_id, selected focus and accepted media authority. A matching opaque handle is only a correlation with the accepted foci configuration; it is not a global Arkret object identity, permission, or Event deduplication key. Existing Call, participant-binding and focus-election proof checks remain mandatory.

applet_install_handle.description: One Applet install operation lifecycle under the exact caller, applet_id and service_id. This response handle does not identify an independent authorization object: registration_event_ref, registration_epoch and the accepted capability/E2EE authorization references prove the installed state. It must not select authorization, replace the registration coordinate, or deduplicate an Event by itself.

agent_rejection_handle.description: One actor-private request-rejection lifecycle under exact (controller AccountId, agent_id, request_id). The handle correlates the rejection outcome; controller authority, signed rejection Event and request target-state CAS determine acceptance. It is not a standalone authorization object, principal identity, or Event deduplication key.

organization_statement_handle.description: Organization endorsement audit lineage under exact (realm_id, organization_id, relationship). statement_id, supersedes_statement_id and revokes_statement_id use the same opaque profile and retain that same scope. They correlate audit/replacement/revocation records, not an external SIWE/OIDC identity or the current-state subject. Authority comes from the original signed Event, accepted organization control and current relationship cut; a handle alone grants no authority and never replaces Event deduplication.
